newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's GAZ names rating adviser.
newsitem.headline: Russia's GAZ names rating adviser.

text.p: Russia's second biggest carmaker AO GAZ said on Friday it had chosen international investment bank CS First Boston as its rating consultant.
"We have signed a contract on rating consultancy with CSFB," a GAZ spokesman told Reuters. He did not give any other details.

Russian newspapers said GAZ was planning to issue $100 million worth of Eurobonds with a maturity of between three and five years in November. They also said Moody's and Standard & Poor's will provide ratings.
The GAZ spokesman said it was too early to talk about the volume or the tenor of the issue.
Previously GAZ President Nikolai Pugin said the company planned to tap international markets with either a Eurobond or shares in autumn.
GAZ produced 209,141 cars, chiefly Volga sedans, in 1996 after 200,292 in 1995. It plans to raise production by 14 percent in 1997.
The company, located in Nizhny Novgorod, owed 550 billion roubles in tax arrears on June 1, 1997.
